seo.title: Landscaping in Colwood, BC — Yards & Grounds Care | RNC
seo.description: Landscape installation, grounds care, irrigation and tree work for Colwood homes and stratas, from Royal Bay new builds to Esquimalt Lagoon.

h1: Landscaping and grounds care in Colwood
summary: Much of Colwood's new housing is in Royal Bay, on land with a century-long history as a gravel operation, so many backyards start from bare new-build ground. Older lots sit near Esquimalt Lagoon, a federal migratory bird sanctuary bordered by old coastal Douglas-fir forest.

Open burning is not allowed in the city at any time, so yard debris is chipped, hauled or taken to the City's Branch Drop Off, which accepts broom, ivy, holly and blackberry. Arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew are protected in Colwood from 2 m tall or 4 cm across.

localRules.text: Removing a protected tree in Colwood needs a Tree Management Permit under Urban Forest Bylaw 1735. You apply online with a Tree Site Plan (five or fewer trees) or a Tree Management Plan, plus photos.
localRules.excerpt: If the tree you are planning to remove is a protected tree, you will need to obtain a Tree Management Permit.

localRules.text: Colwood protects arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew at 2 m tall or 4 cm in diameter; Douglas-fir, grand fir, bigleaf maple and western redcedar at 30 cm in diameter; any tree over 60 cm in diameter at chest height; and retained, replacement and wildlife trees.
localRules.excerpt: Pacific Yew (2m or greater in height OR 4cm or greater in diameter) Douglas Fir (30cm diameter or more)

localRules.text: A Colwood tree permit application needs a Tree Site Plan or Tree Management Plan plus photos; removing more than five protected trees needs a Tree Management Plan by a qualified professional.
localRules.excerpt: If you are cutting more than five protected trees, you will need to provide a Tree Management Plan prepared by a qualified professional.

localRules.text: Colwood replacement trees go on the same lot: one for each tree when one to five are removed, two for each when more than five are removed. They must be at least 1.5 m tall and native to the Coastal Douglas-fir zone. A per-tree security deposit is refunded after the tree survives a year, or a cash-in-lieu payment applies if trees cannot be planted on the lot.
localRules.excerpt: When removing one to five trees, they must be replaced at a 1:1 ratio. When removing more than five trees, they must be replaced at a 2:1 ratio.

localRules.text: Colwood needs no permit for pruning done to sound arboricultural practice. That does not cover lift pruning below a 50% live crown ratio, removing more than 25% of the crown in one season, topping, or cutting a structural root in the critical root zone. Hedges (five or more trees under 5 m tall planted 1.25 m apart) can be pruned or removed without a permit.
localRules.excerpt: removal of more than 25% of the crown in one season, topping, or pruning or removal of a structural root within the critical root zone.

localRules.text: Colwood's Hillside development permit guidelines (posted OCP text marked DRAFT, so check the version in force with the City) say to avoid tree removal on steep slopes, re-vegetate exposed soil on steep slopes with plants native to the Coastal Douglas-fir zone, avoid fast-growing non-native plants for holding soil, and keep windfirm treed buffers between lots.
localRules.sourceTitle: 22. Hillside Environmental DPA (Colwood OCP, DRAFT text)
localRules.excerpt: Avoid tree removal on steep slopes. Trees intercept precipitation and reduce stormwater runoff volumes, protect soils from erosion

localRules.text: Colwood's riparian and marine-shoreline development permit guidelines (posted OCP text marked DRAFT; a 2025 amendment rewrote the riparian guidelines, so check with the City) treat the shoreline as running from the low-tide mark to 11 m above sea level. They set a natural buffer of at least 30 m upland from the natural boundary, do not support shoreline hardening, and keep new structures, including docks, out of the Esquimalt Lagoon Migratory Bird Sanctuary, which includes 100 m from the lagoon's natural boundary.
localRules.sourceTitle: 20. Riparian Areas and Marine Shorelines Environmental DPA (Colwood OCP, DRAFT text)
localRules.excerpt: New structures, including docks, may not be located within the Esquimalt Lagoon Migratory Bird Sanctuary which includes 100 m from the present natural boundary of the Lagoon.

localRules.text: Open burning is not allowed in Colwood at any time: no open yard, beach, camp, land-clearing, demolition or construction-waste fires, so yard debris is chipped or hauled (the City runs a Branch Drop Off). Factory-made outdoor wood-burning appliances with a firebox no larger than 24 by 24 inches are allowed at least 20 ft from buildings, fences, property lines and vegetation, except when the fire rating is High or Extreme.
localRules.excerpt: The City of Colwood prohibits all open yard fires, beach fires and camp fires as well as land clearing, demolition and construction waste fires.

localRules.text: Colwood's Pesticide Use Bylaw generally bars pesticides on lawns, trees, shrubs, flowers and other ornamental plants at homes, duplexes, townhouses, apartments and condominiums. Listed lower-risk products are allowed without a permit, and a permit may be issued for invasive species, noxious weeds or infestations that threaten a sensitive ecosystem. The bylaw does not apply to commercial, institutional or industrial properties.
localRules.excerpt: Pesticide use is generally NOT permitted on lawns and gardens in Colwood

localRules.text: In Colwood, the property owner maintains the boulevard between the lot and the street or sidewalk, keeping grass trimmed and litter cleared. The City asks owners to contact it before changing a boulevard, since plantings or structures are usually not possible over underground utilities.
localRules.excerpt: maintenance of the boulevard between your property and the street or sidewalk in Colwood is the responsibility of the property owner.

localRules.text: In Colwood, removing more than 200 cubic metres of soil or rock off site needs a Blasting Permit and a Soil Deposit Permit (Blasting Bylaw 272). Blasters must notify everyone within 300 m, and blasting is limited to Monday-Thursday 8:30 am-4 pm and Friday 8:30 am-3 pm, with none on weekends or holidays.
localRules.sourceTitle: Blasting & Dust Control - City of Colwood
localRules.excerpt: If a company or developer intends to remove soil and/or rock off site that exceeds 200 cubic meters, a Blasting Permit and Soil Deposit Permit are required

conditions.text: Colwood's Branch Drop Off accepts Scotch broom, English ivy, English holly, Himalayan blackberry, English hawthorn and periwinkle. The City flags poison hemlock, giant hogweed, Japanese knotweed and blessed milk thistle as common culprits.
conditions.excerpt: Know what you can bring to Colwood Branch Drop Off: We CAN ACCEPT: Scotch Broom, English Ivy, English Holly, Himalayan Blackberry, English Hawthorn and Periwinkle.

conditions.text: Colwood offers free FireSmart home assessments to residents through a FireSmart coordinator, with the focus on the Home Ignition Zone, the 30 m around a home.
conditions.excerpt: The area within 30 metres of your home is called the Home Ignition Zone.

conditions.text: Royal Bay has a century-long history as a gravel operation that was one of the region's largest industrial sites, so many Royal Bay yards are new builds on former pit land.
conditions.excerpt: The area has a century-long history as a gravel operation that was one of the region's largest industrial sites and major employers.

conditions.text: Esquimalt Lagoon is a federally designated Migratory Bird Sanctuary managed by the Canadian Wildlife Service, bordered by some of the oldest coastal Douglas-fir forest left in the Victoria area. Waterfront yards nearby sit beside protected habitat.
conditions.excerpt: The lagoon is also bordered by some of the oldest coastal Douglas fir forest remaining in the Victoria area.

proof.text: Hauled a Latoria yard's broom and holly prunings to the Colwood Branch Drop Off instead of stacking a pile no one could burn.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Colwood owners maintain the boulevard between the lot and the street, so regular visits include trimming that strip and clearing litter.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: New-build yards on former pit land often need grading, retaining and planting, and moving more than 200 cubic metres of rock or soil off site needs City permits.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: New lawns and beds in Colwood's subdivisions need systems set up from scratch and tuned to the lawn days for each address.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Hedges of five or more trees under 5 m tall can be pruned or removed in Colwood without a permit, while protected trees need a Tree Management Permit.
